name: GAIN (ExtraTrees fallback)
tagline: Iterative non-linear imputation with ExtraTreesRegressor as the per-feature estimator (numpy GAN GAIN replaced for stability).
pseudocode:
1. Initialise missing entries with column means.
2. Sort features by ascending missingness.
3. for iter $= 1\ldots\text{max\_iter}$ (round-robin):
4.  for each feature $j$ with missing values:
5.   train $\mathrm{ExtraTreesRegressor}(n\_est=100, \max\_features=\sqrt d)$ on observed rows using all other features as predictors.
6.   predict and overwrite missing entries of $j$.
7. Stop when $\|X^{(t)}-X^{(t-1)}\|^2 / \|X^{(t)}\|^2 < 10^{-3}$.
diff_from_baseline: Yoon et al., ICML 2018 — GAIN (Generative Adversarial Imputation Networks). Original GAIN trains a generator/discriminator with hint vectors; this baseline uses sklearn's IterativeImputer + ExtraTrees as a stable non-linear stand-in because the numpy-only GAN cannot backprop through hidden layers.

name: KNN Imputation
tagline: Replace each NaN with the distance-weighted mean of the K=5 nearest complete-feature neighbours.
pseudocode:
1. For each row with NaNs, compute distance to all other rows on commonly observed features.
2. Pick K=5 nearest neighbours.
3. Impute missing entry as the inverse-distance-weighted mean of those neighbours' observed values for that feature.
4. Repeat for every (row, missing feature) pair.
diff_from_baseline: Troyanskaya et al., Bioinformatics 2001. K-Nearest-Neighbour imputation; sklearn.impute.KNNImputer wrapper. Standard non-parametric imputation baseline that uses local feature similarity.

name: MICE (Bayesian Ridge)
tagline: Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations: round-robin Bayesian Ridge regressions on each incomplete feature.
pseudocode:
1. Fill all NaNs with column means as initial guess.
2. Order features by ascending missingness.
3. for iter $= 1\ldots 30$:
4.  for each feature $j$ with missingness:
5.   fit BayesianRidge with $X_{obs,\,\setminus j}$ → $X_{obs,\,j}$.
6.   replace missing entries of $j$ with model's posterior predictions.
7. Stop on tolerance ($10^{-3}$).
diff_from_baseline: van Buuren & Groothuis-Oudshoorn, JSS 2011 — MICE. Round-robin chained-equations imputer; sklearn's IterativeImputer+BayesianRidge implementation. Default mainstream imputation baseline.

name: Mean Imputation
tagline: Replace each missing entry with that column's training mean — the simplest imputation floor.
diff_from_baseline: Standard SimpleImputer(strategy='mean'). Ignores all inter-feature correlations; serves as the floor baseline against which any structured imputer is judged.

name: MissForest
tagline: Iterative Random-Forest imputation: round-robin RF predictions for each incomplete feature until convergence.
pseudocode:
1. Initialise NaNs with column means.
2. Sort features by ascending missingness.
3. for iter $= 1\ldots\text{max\_iter}$:
4.  for each feature $j$ with missingness:
5.   train RandomForestRegressor (n_estimators=100, max_features=√d) on observed rows of $j$ using all other features.
6.   predict and overwrite the missing entries of $j$.
7. Stop when $\|\Delta X\|^2 / \|X\|^2 < 10^{-4}$ or max_iter reached.
diff_from_baseline: Stekhoven & Bühlmann, Bioinformatics 2012 — MissForest. Non-parametric Random-Forest imputation; consistently strong baseline across mixed tabular data and a common SOTA reference.
